findings.claim: Kalindi recalls winning Rs40 for a Mathura-Mangala critical essay encouraged by professor Artaballabha, calling it his first monetary literary prize. He values the teacher’s praise still more.
findings.limit: A literary prize, not a film fee, regular income or livelihood total.

findings.claim: Biswanath Kar accepted his comparative essay despite disagreeing with its judgment of Radhanath and Madhusudan; publication included the editor’s contrary note. Further writing invitations followed.
findings.limit: PDF258 explicitly frames the recalled wording through memory and imagination; not a verbatim contemporary interview or recovered letter.

findings.claim: A handwritten club magazine accommodated Odia, Bengali and English writing; the account follows this collective activity into publishing.
findings.limit: Not evidence of individual earnings, film collaboration or adaptation contracts.

optional_public_candidate.text: Kalindi remembered encouragement as well as publication. A critical essay earned him his first literary prize, but his teacher’s praise mattered more. Later, editor Biswanath Kar printed another essay while disagreeing with its argument—a recollection of editorial generosity rather than agreement.
optional_public_candidate.status: Initial-range optional candidate only. Coordinator may prefer extension’s character-origin or working-method detail; do not automatically adopt multiple paragraphs.

Writing with a scribe supplies a concrete working-method detail. Preserve unresolved adaptation remuneration; do not turn the house-building criticism into earnings evidence.
